2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioners as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 281 of 2008 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Narsingdi Sadar, Narsingdi against the opposite parties as defendant for a decree of partition of the suit land with declaration of title stating inter alia, that the schedule `ka' and `kha' property belonged to the father of the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 who died leaving the plaintiffs, defendant No.1 and his wife Gulesa Khatun, Subsequently, Gulesa Khatun died leaving the plaintiffs and defendant No.1. According to the plaint the properties mentioned in schedule `kha' have already been amicably partitioned among the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 as per their share and entitlement. The record of right for the properties mentioned in schedule `kha' have been correctly recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 and they have been possessing the said land without any dispute. Out of the schedule "kha" land the plaintiffs as well as the defendant No.1 transferred major portion of the property to different persons. Since the property mentioned in schedule `kha' correctly recorded according to share of the plaintiff and defendant No.1, and they got the same amicably partitioned no prayer for partition of the schedule `kha' is necessary. Property mentioned in schedule `ka' to the plaint covered by SA khatian No. 54, plot No. 50 corresponding to RS khatian No. 27 and plot Nos. 53, 226 and 231 measuring 83 sataks remains in ejmali for which the plaintiffs filed the instant suit for partition as per their shares. 

 7. Mr Md Sagir Anwar with M. Mushfiqur Rahman, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submit that the appellate court while allowing the appeal mainly considered two aspects; that the suit is barred by defect of parties and hotchpotch. Mr Sagir further submits that the property mentioned in schedule `ka' to the plaint is the property of the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 accordingly, present RS khatian stand recorded in their names. Except the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 there are no other co-sharers in the suit plots, therefore, findings and observations of the appellate court to the effect that the suit is barred by defect of parties is absolutely contrary to the actual state of affairs. 

 9. Mr Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate with Mr Swapan Kumar Mitra learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 submit that it is the general rule that a partition suit should include all the joint properties of the parties concerned and all the person who are co-sharer in the holding have to be made party but in the instant suit admittedly the plaintiffs did not prayed for saham bringing all the properties left by their father Abdul Malek and all the persons whose name appearing in the khatian have not been made parties to the suit and, as such, the appellate court rightly found and observed that the suit is barred by defect of parties and hotchpotch. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Nurul Afsar vs Rafiqul Ahmed, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 155, Laksman Mondal vs Laksmi Dasi reported in 10 DLR 27. 

 12. Admittedly, the property under partition originally belonged to one Abdul Malek, who died leaving the plaintiffs as daughter and defendant No.1 as only son. As per Muslim laws of inheritance the plaintiffs are entitled to eight annas shares in the property left by their father. In the instant suit the plaintiffs sought partition from the property mentioned in schedule 'ka' only. In respect of schedule `kha' land the plaintiffs clearly stated and asserted that those properties have already been partitioned among the heirs of Abdul Malek by metes and bound. It is also admitted by both the parties that the property mentioned in schedule `kha' have been amicably partitioned according to their share and some of the property under schedule `kha' have already been transferred by plaintiffs and defendant No. 1 to different persons against which both the parties have had no claim and objection whatsoever. The defendant in suit in his written statement as well as examination in chief did not mention and or state even a single word that the plaintiffs amicably got their share from other properties in exchange of shares in schedule 'ka' property. It is also not a claim or case of the defendant No.1 that the plaintiffs sold out any property from schedule `kha' in excess of their share or entitlement to any person disentitling them to claim further share from schedule `ka' land. It is also not a case of the defendant No.1 that the properties under schedule 'kha' were not partitioned amicably as stated by the plaintiffs or he prays for saham from schedule 'kha'. In the absence of any definite case on the part of the defendant No.1 and any evidence to the effect that the defendant No.1 got the property under schedule `ka.' by amicable arrangement during life time of their father Abdul Malek claim of the plaintiffs to the extent of eight annas share in the schedule `Ka' property cannot be negated under any circumstances. From perusal of RS khatian No. 27 it appears that the same stands recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 and, as such, the findings of the appellate court that the suit is barred by defect of parties is contrary to the actual state of affairs and the evidences on record.
